description: Representative canonical governance manifest for the synthetic Keystone Motion Components dataset. Defines canonical entities, keys, and write-path invariants enforced by Yggdrasil ERP at the point of commit. This is illustrative of the enforcement model, not a production schema.
principles: Invariants are bound to business state, not to a screen, workflow, endpoint, or caller identity.
Every write path (UI, API, bulk import, service account, autonomous agent) is validated by the same invariants.
Invalid state is refused before commit; it is never persisted and then flagged.
Provenance is a first-class part of a transaction, not an attachment discovered after the fact.

validation_outcomes.reject_invalid_approval: A referenced CustomerApprovalArtifact does not authorize this specific change.
validation_outcomes.reject_ambiguous_field: The approval artifact does not name the field, order, or values it purports to authorize.
validation_outcomes.reject_mismatched_date: The approval's previous/proposed values do not match the transaction's from/to values.
validation_outcomes.reject_missing_provenance: A controlled field was changed without a complete, validated provenance chain.
validation_outcomes.reject_alias_collision: An entity reference resolves to an unresolved or unmapped alias rather than a canonical entity.

canonical_entities.identity_rule: One canonical record per legal customer. Surface names and codes are aliases requiring resolution; duplicate codes (e.g. NSDS on CUST-1001 and CUST-1005) must be merged before commit of dependent transactions.

One canonical record per physical part. Free-text part numbers coined by inventory, receiving, or quality systems are aliases and must resolve to a single canonical part_id before any transaction referencing them commits.
One canonical record per legal supplier. Surface names are aliases; an alias must be resolved to a canonical supplier_id (resolution confidence 1.0) before it can act as supplier-of-record.

strict_invariant.name: requested_ship_date_change_requires_matching_approval
strict_invariant.statement: RequestedShipDate on a SalesOrder cannot be changed unless the committing transaction includes a valid CustomerApprovalArtifact whose fields match the change exactly.
match_conditions: approval.approval_author is a recognized customer contact
approval.source_document_id or approval.source_document_hash is present and verifiable

invariants: semantic_validation must be one of the validation_outcomes and may never be 'not_evaluated' for a committed state change
every committed state change carries the validated provenance that authorized it
canonical_entities.note: In the enforced model the audit event records not only that a change occurred but the validation verdict that permitted it. An event can exist only because a valid transaction produced it.
